claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
The work Gesta cum Emerito (Proceedings with Emeritus) was written in AD 418.

The encounter took place on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October in the consulship of Honorius for the twelfth time and Theodosius for the eighth time, in the major church at Caesarea, with multiple bishops present including Deuterius metropolitan of Caesarea, Alypius of Thagaste, Possidius of Calama, Rusticus of Cartenna, and Palladius of Thiabe, as well as presbyters, deacons, clergy, and a great crowd.
Emeritus was the Donatist bishop of Caesarea (ancient Cherchell).

The work records Augustine's attempt to engage Emeritus in debate about the Donatist schism, and Augustine shaped the account to highlight Donatist inconsistencies, particularly their treatment of Maximianists at the 394 synod in Bagaï where Emeritus had condemned Maximian.

In the Gesta cum Emerito, Augustine had Alypius read out passages of Aurelius' 411 letter to Marcellinus the imperial commissioner (Epistula 128), reliving arguments from the earlier 411 confrontation.

The Donatist controversy arose from the Diocletianic persecutions in the early fourth century, when the Donatists split from Catholics over whether the church must retain purity by separating from sinners or could tolerate sinners' presence; Donatists also regarded sacraments administered by sinful clergy as invalid.

Augustine's memory of the 411 confrontation with Emeritus was dynamic, and his continued revisiting of the same ground years after 411 demonstrates his determination to overcome Donatist resistance by intellectual persuasion and conversion as well as by judicial victory and imperial enforcement.
The text survives as a published account of the proceedings, edited by Petschenig in 1910.
